spec.description: Client-side performance telemetry (channel boxel:client-perf) re-emitted by realm-server as structured JSON log lines and read from Loki. Overview headline signals plus a collapsible row per event type; the User/Session variables drill the whole board into a single client.

panels.description: Card loads completed within the last 5 minutes of the selected time range — the number is the latest 5-minute count, the sparkline is how that count moved across the range. A card load is one "Loading card…" window resolving.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:client-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:client-perf" | event_type="card-load" | matrix_user_id=~"$matrix_user_id" | session_id=~".*${session_id}.*" [5m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Card loads (5m)

panels.description: Main-thread freezes of 10s or more within the last 5 minutes of the selected time range — the number is the latest 5-minute count, the sparkline is how freezes were distributed across the range. Anything non-zero is worth the wedge row below; sub-second jank lives in keepalive max_gap_ms instead.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:client-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:client-perf" | event_type="wedge" | matrix_user_id=~"$matrix_user_id" | session_id=~".*${session_id}.*" [5m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Wedges ≥10s (5m)

panels.description: Loader/store rebuilds within the last 5 minutes of the selected time range — the number is the latest 5-minute count, the sparkline is how rebuilds were distributed across the range. Counts both sources: rebuilds driven by incoming index events and the write-time re-establishment a code-mode save performs.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:client-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:client-perf" | event_type="rebuild" | matrix_user_id=~"$matrix_user_id" | session_id=~".*${session_id}.*" [5m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Rebuilds (5m)

panels.description: p95 card-to-interactive latency (card-load settle_ms) alongside p95 server-request duration_ms. The headline responsiveness signals.

panels.title: Signal event rate (events / interval)

panels.description: Active sessions over the selected time range, stacked by account: at each point, how many sessions each user had active in the preceding 5m. Total stack height is concurrency, the colours are who, and the legend doubles as the current-user list. The grey "build in use" legend rows name the host build(s) the active sessions run (from the app_version every beacon stamps): one row means every session is on that build; a second row right after a deploy is a tab that has not reloaded and still runs the previous code. Hovering the chart names which user is on which build. One session is one browser tab. The hover attribution is a third query byte-identical to the bands query, differing only in display name — Grafana cannot vary legend and tooltip names independently, so deleting the "duplicate" removes the user → build hover.

targets.expr: count by (matrix_user_id, app_version) (count by (matrix_user_id, app_version, session_id) (count_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:client-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:client-perf" | matrix_user_id=~"$matrix_user_id" | session_id=~".*${session_id}.*" [5m])))

count by (matrix_user_id, app_version) (count by (matrix_user_id, app_version, session_id) (count_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:client-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:client-perf" | matrix_user_id=~"$matrix_user_id" | session_id=~".*${session_id}.*" [5m])))

By user — who is hitting issues

panels.description: Main-thread freezes at or above the wedge threshold, by the account that suffered them and the script frame that was blocking (`fn @ url:char` — the char offset source-map-resolves even for minified builds). The frame is what makes a row actionable: it names the code that held the thread. A blank frame is a freeze corroborated only by a longtask, with no LoAF script attribution — real, and its blocked time can read 0, which is why rows also carry a wedge count and the limit sits far above any plausible row count: every wedging user stays on the board. Worst blocked ms is the single worst freeze for that user+frame.

targets.expr: topk(200, max by (matrix_user_id, top_frame_function, top_frame_url) (max_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:client-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:client-perf" | matrix_user_id=~"$matrix_user_id" | session_id=~".*${session_id}.*" | event_type="wedge" | unwrap blocked_ms [$__range])))

topk(200, sum by (matrix_user_id, top_frame_function, top_frame_url) (count_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:client-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:client-perf" | matrix_user_id=~"$matrix_user_id" | session_id=~".*${session_id}.*" | event_type="wedge" [$__range])))

panels.title: Wedges by user

panels.description: The slowest card-to-interactive each account experienced, named by the card that was slow — settle_ms is the "Loading card…" window the user sat through. The card id is the why: it says which card to open the card-load row for, and repeated rows for one card across users point at the card, not the network.

targets.expr: topk(25, max by (matrix_user_id, card_id) (max_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:client-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:client-perf" | matrix_user_id=~"$matrix_user_id" | session_id=~".*${session_id}.*" | event_type="card-load" | unwrap settle_ms [$__range])))

panels.title: Worst card-to-interactive by user (max settle_ms)

panels.description: What kind of signals each account is generating — volume alone is not a problem (an active user loads many cards), so the mix is the read: wedges are freezes, rebuilds are code-change absorption cost, server-request and deserialize columns rise with ordinary activity. A user whose column weight sits in wedge/rebuild is having a bad time; one whose weight is card-load is just busy.

targets.expr: sum by (matrix_user_id, event_type) (count_over_time({service="realm-server", env="$env"} |= "boxel:client-perf" | json | line_format "{{ if .log }}{{ .log }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}" | json | channel="boxel:client-perf" | matrix_user_id=~"$matrix_user_id" | session_id=~".*${session_id}.*" | event_type!="keepalive" [$__range]))
